todaysEvents.summary: US 7th night strikes expand to infrastructure
todaysEvents.delta: Up: CENTCOM launched 7th consecutive night of strikes against Iran (Jul 18), expanding beyond purely military targets to bridges near Bandar Abbas, the tower at Chabahar port, and electrical power infrastructure (AP, Jul 18; RFE/RL, Jul 18). The highway and railway bridge strikes appeared aimed at cutting off Bandar Abbas from roads into Iran's central region. US acknowledged 13 additional service members injured since Monday.

Up: Iranian Maj. Gen. Mohsen Rezaei threatened Tehran is ready to resume 'full-scale offensive operations' if US strikes continue for another 2-3 days, warning 'no political border will be safe' (IRIB/AP, Jul 18). Iran retaliated by striking a Kuwait water desalination plant, and targeting Qatar, Bahrain, and Jordan with missiles.

todaysEvents.summary: Hormuz traffic at 3-week low; Brent surges
todaysEvents.delta: Up: Shipping through Hormuz fell to 8 transits on Jul 16, lowest in 3 weeks and down from 15 the previous day and >100 prewar (Kpler/CNBC, Jul 17). Brent surged to $88.09 (+5.75%, Yahoo Finance Jul 18) as supply disruption fears intensified. TTF jumped to €59.03 (+7.51%, Trading Economics Jul 17). 'Worst case scenario' for oil tankers per Marisks CEO (CNBC, Jul 17).

scenarios.label: Base
scenarios.description: A diplomatic off-ramp remains highly unlikely after Trump's blockade and tribute order and the expansion of US strikes to infrastructure targets. No talks have materialized. Any resumption of negotiations would require Iran to accept both the blockade and the 20% cargo fee, which Tehran has already rejected. Brent would settle toward $85-95/bbl as risk premium partially deflates. Probability held at 10%.

scenarios.label: Stress
scenarios.description: Hormuz blockade continues with sporadic enforcement; Iranian strikes persist at a constrained tempo. US strikes expanding to infrastructure targets (bridges, port tower, power) signal a broader campaign. Iran's threat of full-scale offensive operations if strikes continue 2-3 more days raises the ceiling on this scenario. Brent trades $100-130/bbl, JKM surges toward $25-30/MMBtu, iTraxx Asia IG breaks 150bp. Probability reduced to 20% as tail scenario becomes more likely.

scenarios.label: Tail
scenarios.description: Conflict widens as US strikes now target Iranian infrastructure beyond purely military sites. Iran follows through on full-scale offensive operations threat, expanding the war beyond Gulf states to new geographies. Kuwait's water desalination plant already damaged. Brent spikes $115-140+/bbl with sustained outages; JKM above $35/MMBtu; Asian credit markets dislocate. Probability raised to 70% reflecting infrastructure escalation and full-scale ops threat.
